claims.statement: Higher aggregate performance in multi-agent setups can coexist with hidden task degradation and lower non-degradation bounds.

support.explanation: Demonstrates that group or aggregate consensus metrics do not guarantee uniform reliability across all constituent tasks.
support.passage: Our experiments show that higher hidden-task accuracy can coexist with more counterexamples to non-degradation and lower non-degradation bounds.

actions.reason: Synthesizing collected evidence to evaluate consensus reliability versus independent epistemic monitoring.
actions.summary: This synthesis examines how aggregate performance gains in multi-agent debate and consensus paradigms can conceal selective hidden-task degradation, raising questions about blindly trusting group consensus over verifiable individual reliability.
actions.title: Epistemic Reliability and Consensus Limitations in Multi-Agent Systems
